_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Belize covering Early Maya (Cuello ~2500 BCE), Classic Maya cities (Caracol, Xunantunich, Lamanai, Altun Ha), Maya resistance to Spanish, Baymen/logwood era, Battle of St. George's Caye 1798, British Honduras colony, mahogany trade, Hurricane Hattie 1961 (capital moved to Belmopan), independence 1981, George Price (Father of the Nation), Guatemala territorial claim, and Belize Barrier Reef.

religion.note: Catholic majority (Spanish/Maya/Mestizo heritage); Pentecostal/Adventist growing; Anglican (British legacy); Mennonite communities; Maya traditional religion; Garifuna spiritual practices (dugu)

ethnic_groups.name: Mestizo
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed Maya-Spanish; largest group (growing due to Central American immigration); Spanish-speaking; concentrated in north and west; Yucatecan refugees from Caste War 1847

ethnic_groups.name: Creole (Kriol)
ethnic_groups.notes: African-European descent; English Creole speakers; historically dominant in Belize City; Belizean Kriol culture; declining percentage as mestizo immigration grows

ethnic_groups.name: Maya
ethnic_groups.notes: Q'eqchi' (south), Mopan (west), Yucatec (north); descendants of Classic Maya civilization; Caracol/Xunantunich/Lamanai; land rights issues; some undercounted

ethnic_groups.name: Garifuna
ethnic_groups.notes: African-Carib-Arawak descent; arrived from St. Vincent 1832; Dangriga, Hopkins, Punta Gorda; punta music; UNESCO intangible heritage; unique language/culture

ethnic_groups.name: East Indian
ethnic_groups.notes: Descendants of indentured workers from India

ethnic_groups.name: Mennonite
ethnic_groups.notes: German-speaking; arrived 1958; farming communities (Spanish Lookout, Shipyard); major agricultural producers; Plautdietsch; distinctive dress

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Chinese, Lebanese, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Chinese (growing, restaurant/retail); Lebanese; small expatriate community

country_profile.notes_unique: Only English-speaking country in Central America; Belize Barrier Reef (UNESCO, largest in Western Hemisphere); Great Blue Hole; Maya ruins (Caracol defeated mighty Tikal); Battle of St. George's Caye 1798 (national holiday); capital moved to Belmopan after Hurricane Hattie 1961 destroyed Belize City; Guatemala territorial claim (ongoing, half of Belize); Mennonite farmers; jaguar preserve (world's first); diverse multilingual society

current_leader.name: King Charles III
current_leader.title: Monarch (Head of State)
current_leader.notes: Represented by Governor-General Dame Froyla Tzalam (first Maya Governor-General, since 2021)

prime_minister.name: Johnny Briceño
prime_minister.title: Prime Minister
prime_minister.notes: PUP; mestizo from Orange Walk; businessman; COVID recovery; Guatemala ICJ case; re-elected on anti-corruption platform

former_leaders.name: Dean Barrow
former_leaders.notes: UDP; first Black PM; nationalizations (BEL, BTL); three terms; lawyer; anti-corruption rhetoric

former_leaders.name: Said Musa
former_leaders.notes: PUP; Palestinian descent; infrastructure development; financial scandals; social spending

former_leaders.name: Manuel Esquivel
former_leaders.notes: UDP; free-market reforms; privatization; two non-consecutive terms

former_leaders.name: George Price
former_leaders.notes: Father of the Nation; PUP; led Belize to independence 1981; 30+ years in politics; mestizo-Creole; Catholic; humble 'George' identity; self-government 1964

910.name: Early Maya Civilisation in Belize
910.description: Preclassic Maya settlement in Belize: Cuello, Lamanai, Cerros, and early village agriculture.

sub_clusters.name: Cuello — Earliest Maya Village
sub_clusters.description: One of the earliest known Maya sites, pottery traditions, maize agriculture in northern Belize.

sub_clusters.name: Lamanai Preclassic Development
sub_clusters.description: Major centre on the New River Lagoon, monumental architecture, jaguar iconography, continuous occupation.

sub_clusters.name: Cerros and Maritime Trade
sub_clusters.description: Coastal trading centre in Corozal district, early divine kingship, temple façade masks.

920.name: Classic Maya Cities of Belize
920.description: Flourishing Maya city-states: Caracol rivals Tikal, Xunantunich, Altun Ha, Lubaantun.

sub_clusters.name: Caracol — Maya Superpower
sub_clusters.description: Largest Maya site in Belize, defeat of Tikal in 562 CE, Caana sky-palace, population over 100,000.

sub_clusters.name: Xunantunich and Altun Ha
sub_clusters.description: Xunantunich's El Castillo frieze; Altun Ha's jade head of Kinich Ahau, trade gateway.

sub_clusters.name: Lamanai — Classic to Postclassic Continuity
sub_clusters.description: Rare continuous Maya occupation through the collapse, Spanish mission resistance.

930.name: Spanish Contact and British Settlement
930.description: Spanish claims, Maya resistance, English and Scottish logwood cutters, baymen settlement.

sub_clusters.name: Spanish Encounters and Maya Resistance
sub_clusters.description: Spanish contact, Lamanai mission, Maya rebellions, Spain's loose control of the interior.

sub_clusters.name: Baymen and the Logwood Era
sub_clusters.description: English buccaneers-turned-logwood cutters settle Belize River, enslaved African labour, pirate origins.

sub_clusters.name: Battle of St. George's Caye
sub_clusters.description: Baymen and enslaved allies defeat Spanish naval force, securing British control of the territory.

940.name: British Honduras Colony
940.description: Formal colonization, mahogany trade, Garifuna arrival, Caste War refugees, crown colony status.

sub_clusters.name: Mahogany Trade and Plantation Economy
sub_clusters.description: Transition from logwood to mahogany, enslaved and later free Black labour, forestry-based economy.

sub_clusters.name: Garifuna Arrival and Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Garifuna people settle Dangriga and Punta Gorda after exile from St. Vincent, rich cultural contribution.

sub_clusters.name: Crown Colony Status
sub_clusters.description: Formally declared Crown Colony of British Honduras (1862), colonial administration, limited self-rule.

950.name: Twentieth-Century British Honduras
950.description: Great Depression, labour unrest, hurricane devastation, emergence of nationalist movement.

sub_clusters.name: Labour Unrest and Depression
sub_clusters.description: Ex-servicemen riots (1919), Great Depression impact on mahogany and chicle industries, early unions.

sub_clusters.name: Hurricane Hattie and Capital Move
sub_clusters.description: Category 5 Hurricane Hattie devastates Belize City (1961), decision to build new capital at Belmopan.

sub_clusters.name: Self-Government Movement
sub_clusters.description: People's United Party (PUP) founded, George Price leads independence movement, self-governance (1964).

950.name: Road to Independence
950.description: Internal self-government, Guatemala territorial claim, British garrison, independence achieved.

sub_clusters.name: George Price and National Identity
sub_clusters.description: George Price, 'Father of the Nation', leads through decolonisation, multiculturalism, and independence.

sub_clusters.name: Guatemala Territorial Claim
sub_clusters.description: Guatemala's claim to all of Belize, military threats, British deterrent, UN support for Belizean sovereignty.

sub_clusters.name: Independence Day — 21 September 1981
sub_clusters.description: Belize achieves independence with British military guarantee; George Price becomes first PM.

960.name: Post-Independence Belize
960.description: Democratic consolidation, PUP-UDP alternation, continued Guatemalan dispute, economic challenges.

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Alternation (PUP–UDP)
sub_clusters.description: Peaceful transfers of power, Esquivel and Musa governments, democratic stability.

sub_clusters.name: Barrier Reef and Conservation
sub_clusters.description: Belize Barrier Reef UNESCO site (1996), petroleum moratorium, marine reserves, ecotourism.

960.name: Contemporary Belize
960.description: ICJ referral of Guatemala dispute, Briceño government, climate vulnerability, post-COVID recovery.

sub_clusters.name: Guatemala–Belize ICJ Referral
sub_clusters.description: 2018 twin referendums, ICJ case accepted, ongoing proceedings at The Hague.

sub_clusters.name: Climate and Small-State Challenges
sub_clusters.description: Sea-level rise, coral bleaching, hurricane exposure, tourism dependence, COVID-19 impact.

sub_clusters.name: Belizean Multicultural Identity
sub_clusters.description: Creole, Maya, Garifuna, Mestizo, Mennonite mosaic; Kriol language, punta music, cultural festivals.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
